correctness.rationale: Conditioned on nondegenerate lengths, pair inner products have variance 1/d and zero pairwise cross covariance. Gaussian polar coupling G_i=sqrt(d)R_iU_i yields H_d=d^-1/2 sum_h Y_h, iid variance-one Gaussian quadratic forms with trB=0, 2tr(B²)=1 and EY_h⁴=3+48tr(B⁴)<=15. Standard Wasserstein Stein bound gives 3*15^(3/4)/sqrt(d); independent radii and pair orthogonality give exact mean-square comparison 2Var(||G||/sqrt(d))<=2/d. Triangle bound <25/sqrt(d) uniformly in n and weights. Independent matrix checks on four weight arrays found 3*15^.75+sqrt2=24.280187229<25. No step-length moment assumptions are used except finite entries and Q>0.
residual_risks: Unstated constants of general Stein inequality assumed standard; theorem is W1, not total variation or almost-sure coupling.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 Pearson walk primary source (Theorems 4.3/5.4, Lemma 5.3) gives first-order radius convergence and moment bounds, not conditional standard-normal W1 approximation at a dimension-only rate uniform in arbitrarily growing number of weighted steps. Fixed/equal-length radial CLTs are recognized special cases; present theorem strictly adds arbitrary dependent realized lengths and quantitative uniformity.
residual_risks: A general Stein second-chaos normal-approximation theorem may imply the present bound abstractly; novelty of the precise uniform conditional statement remains best-of-knowledge.

value.rationale: A genuinely useful quantitative CLT for a canonical random-walk radial statistic with an explicit dimension-only rate, no restrictions on the number of steps and no moments/dependence assumptions on the length vector. This strengthens known first-order asymptotics and supplies a robust reusable estimate, beyond a textbook fixed-n special case.
residual_risks: Uniformity still depends crucially on independent uniformly spherical directions and Q(L)>0.
